questions.stem: A shopkeeper bought an article for Rs. \(800\) and sold it at a profit of \(25\)%. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.keySolution:
Given: Cost price = Rs. \(800\), Profit = \(25\)%
Selling price = Cost price + Profit
Selling price = \(800 + \frac{25}{100} \times 800 = 800 + 200 = 1000\)
Therefore, selling price = Rs. \(1000\)

questions.stem: An article is sold at Rs. \(720\), making a loss of \(20\)%. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.keySolution:
Given: Selling price = Rs. \(720\), Loss = \(20\)%
Let cost price = \(x\)
Selling price = Cost price - Loss
\(720 = x - \frac{20}{100} \times x = x - 0.2x = 0.8x\)
\(x = \frac{720}{0.8} = 900\)
Therefore, cost price = Rs. \(900\)

questions.stem: A trader marks his goods \(40\)% above the cost price and gives a discount of \(15\)%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = Rs. \(100\)
Marked price = \(100 + 40 = 140\)
Discount = \(15\)% of \(140 = \frac{15}{100} \times 140 = 21\)
Selling price = \(140 - 21 = 119\)
Profit = \(119 - 100 = 19\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{19}{100} \times 100 = 19\)%

questions.stem: Two successive discounts of \(20\)% and \(15\)% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.keySolution:
Let marked price = Rs. \(100\)
After first discount of \(20\)%: \(100 - 20 = 80\)
After second discount of \(15\)% on \(80\): \(80 - \frac{15}{100} \times 80 = 80 - 12 = 68\)
Total discount = \(100 - 68 = 32\)
Single discount = \(32\)%

questions.stem: A shopkeeper sells \(20\) articles for the cost price of \(25\) articles. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price of each article = Re. \(1\)
Cost price of \(20\) articles = Rs. \(20\)
Selling price of \(20\) articles = Cost price of \(25\) articles = Rs. \(25\)
Profit = \(25 - 20 = 5\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{5}{20} \times 100 = 25\)%

questions.stem: A dishonest dealer uses a weight of \(900\) grams instead of \(1\) kg and sells at cost price. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
He gives \(900\) grams for the price of \(1000\) grams
Cost price = \(900\) grams, Selling price = \(1000\) grams (in terms of price)
Profit = \(1000 - 900 = 100\) grams
Profit percentage = \(\frac{100}{900} \times 100 = 11.11\)%

questions.stem: If the selling price of \(15\) articles is equal to the cost price of \(20\) articles, find the profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price of each article = Re. \(1\)
Cost price of \(15\) articles = Rs. \(15\)
Selling price of \(15\) articles = Cost price of \(20\) articles = Rs. \(20\)
Profit = \(20 - 15 = 5\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{5}{15} \times 100 = 33.33\)%

questions.stem: A man buys eggs at \(3\) for Rs. \(5\) and sells at \(5\) for Rs. \(12\). Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \(3\) eggs = Rs. \(5\), so cost price of \(1\) egg = Rs. \(\frac{5}{3}\)
Selling price of \(5\) eggs = Rs. \(12\), so selling price of \(1\) egg = Rs. \(\frac{12}{5}\)
For \(15\) eggs (LCM of \(3\) and \(5\)):
Cost price = \(15 \times \frac{5}{3} = 25\)
Selling price = \(15 \times \frac{12}{5} = 36\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{36-25}{25} \times 100 = 44\)%

questions.stem: A shopkeeper allows a discount of \(10\)% on the marked price. If he still makes a profit of \(17\)%, find the marked price as a percentage of cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = Rs. \(100\)
Selling price = \(100 + 17 = 117\) (profit of \(17\)%)
Let marked price = \(x\)
After \(10\)% discount: \(x - \frac{10x}{100} = 0.9x = 117\)
\(x = \frac{117}{0.9} = 130\)
Marked price as percentage of cost price = \(\frac{130}{100} \times 100 = 130\)%

questions.stem: By selling an article for Rs. \(900\), a man loses \(10\)%. At what price should he sell to gain \(15\)%?
questions.keySolution:
Given: Selling price = Rs. \(900\), Loss = \(10\)%
Cost price = \(\frac{900}{1 - 0.10} = \frac{900}{0.90} = 1000\)
For \(15\)% gain:
Required selling price = \(1000 + \frac{15}{100} \times 1000 = 1000 + 150 = 1150\)
Therefore, required selling price = Rs. \(1150\)

questions.stem: A trader gives \(1\) free article on buying every \(10\) articles and gains \(20\)%. Find the marked price as a percentage of cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Customer pays for \(10\) articles but gets \(11\) articles
Let cost price of each article = Rs. \(1\)
Cost price of \(11\) articles = Rs. \(11\)
Selling price of \(10\) articles = Rs. \(11 \times 1.20 = 13.20\) (\(20\)% gain)
Marked price of \(1\) article = \(\frac{13.20}{10} = 1.32\)
Marked price as percentage of cost price = \(\frac{1.32}{1} \times 100 = 132\)%

questions.stem: The cost price of \(20\) articles is equal to the selling price of \(16\) articles. Find the profit or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let selling price of each article = Re. \(1\)
Selling price of \(16\) articles = Rs. \(16\)
Cost price of \(20\) articles = Rs. \(16\)
Cost price of \(1\) article = Rs. \(\frac{16}{20} = 0.8\)
Loss per article = \(1 - 0.8 = 0.2\)
Loss percentage = \(\frac{0.2}{1} \times 100 = 20\)%
Wait, let me recalculate:
Cost price of \(16\) articles = \(16 \times 0.8 = 12.8\)
Selling price of \(16\) articles = \(16\)
Profit = \(16 - 12.8 = 3.2\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{3.2}{12.8} \times 100 = 25\)%

questions.stem: A shopkeeper bought \(200\) mangoes at Rs. \(10\) each. \(20\)% of them got spoiled. At what rate per mango should he sell the remaining to get \(25\)% overall profit?
questions.keySolution:
Total cost price = \(200 \times 10 = 2000\)
Spoiled mangoes = \(20\)% of \(200 = 40\)
Remaining mangoes = \(200 - 40 = 160\)
For \(25\)% profit, required selling price = \(2000 \times 1.25 = 2500\)
Selling price per mango = \(\frac{2500}{160} = 15.625\)
Therefore, selling price per mango = Rs. \(15.625\)

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for Rs. \(2400\) each. One is sold at \(20\)% profit and other at \(20\)% loss. Find the overall profit or loss percentage.
A dealer marks his goods at \(50\)% above cost price and allows successive discounts of \(20\)% and \(10\)%. Find his profit or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = Rs. \(100\)
Marked price = \(100 + 50 = 150\)
After first discount of \(20\)%: \(150 \times 0.80 = 120\)
After second discount of \(10\)%: \(120 \times 0.90 = 108\)
Selling price = Rs. \(108\)
Profit = \(108 - 100 = 8\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{8}{100} \times 100 = 8\)%

questions.stem: A man sells two watches for Rs. \(1980\) each. On one he gains \(10\)% and on the other he loses \(10\)%. Find his overall gain or loss percentage.
If the cost price increases by \(25\)% but selling price remains same, the profit decreases by Rs. \(50\). If original profit was \(25\)%, find the original cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let original cost price = \(x\)
Original selling price = \(x + 0.25x = 1.25x\)
New cost price = \(x + 0.25x = 1.25x\)
New profit = \(1.25x - 1.25x = 0\)
Decrease in profit = \(0.25x - 0 = 0.25x = 50\)
Therefore, \(x = \frac{50}{0.25} = 200\)
Original cost price = Rs. \(200\)

questions.stem: A grocer mixes \(30\) kg of wheat costing Rs. \(9.50\) per kg with \(20\) kg of wheat costing Rs. \(8.75\) per kg. At what rate per kg should he sell the mixture to gain \(16\)%?
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \(30\) kg wheat = \(30 \times 9.50 = 285\)
Cost of \(20\) kg wheat = \(20 \times 8.75 = 175\)
Total cost = \(285 + 175 = 460\)
Total quantity = \(30 + 20 = 50\) kg
Cost price per kg = \(\frac{460}{50} = 9.20\)
For \(16\)% gain, selling price per kg = \(9.20 \times 1.16 = 10.672\)
Therefore, selling price = Rs. \(10.64\) per kg (rounded)

questions.stem: A retailer buys \(40\) pens at Rs. \(36\) per dozen and sells them at Rs. \(4.50\) each. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Number of dozens = \(\frac{40}{12} = \frac{10}{3}\)
Cost price = \(\frac{10}{3} \times 36 = 120\)
Selling price = \(40 \times 4.50 = 180\)
Profit = \(180 - 120 = 60\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{60}{120} \times 100 = 50\)%

questions.stem: A merchant sells an article at \(8\)% loss. If he had sold it for Rs. \(169\) more, he would have gained \(7\)%. Find the cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(x\)
Selling price at \(8\)% loss = \(x - 0.08x = 0.92x\)
Selling price at \(7\)% gain = \(x + 0.07x = 1.07x\)
Difference = \(1.07x - 0.92x = 0.15x = 169\)
Therefore, \(x = \frac{169}{0.15} = 1126.67 \approx 1130\)
Cost price = Rs. \(1130\)

questions.stem: A man bought some apples at \(6\) for Rs. \(10\) and sold them at \(4\) for Rs. \(9\). Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \(6\) apples = Rs. \(10\)
Cost price of \(1\) apple = Rs. \(\frac{10}{6} = \frac{5}{3}\)
Selling price of \(4\) apples = Rs. \(9\)
Selling price of \(1\) apple = Rs. \(\frac{9}{4}\)
For LCM of \(6\) and \(4\) = \(12\) apples:
Cost price = \(12 \times \frac{5}{3} = 20\)
Selling price = \(12 \times \frac{9}{4} = 27\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{27-20}{20} \times 100 = 35\)%

questions.stem: If by selling an article for Rs. \(390\), a trader loses \(25\)%, for how much should he sell it to gain \(25\)%?
questions.keySolution:
Given: SP = Rs. \(390\), Loss = \(25\)%
Cost price = \(\frac{390}{1-0.25} = \frac{390}{0.75} = 520\)
For \(25\)% gain:
Required selling price = \(520 \times 1.25 = 650\)
Therefore, required selling price = Rs. \(650\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper uses faulty weights. He sells at cost price but uses \(850\) grams weight instead of \(1\) kg. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
He gives \(850\) grams for the price of \(1000\) grams
Cost of goods = \(850\) grams
Price received = equivalent to \(1000\) grams
Profit = \(1000 - 850 = 150\) grams worth
Profit percentage = \(\frac{150}{850} \times 100 = 17.65\)%

questions.stem: The ratio of cost price to selling price of an article is \(4:5\). Find the profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Given ratio CP : SP = \(4 : 5\)
Let CP = \(4x\) and SP = \(5x\)
Profit = \(5x - 4x = x\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{x}{4x} \times 100 = 25\)%

questions.stem: A dealer allows \(16\)% discount on the marked price and still makes \(12\)% profit. If the cost price is Rs. \(150\), find the marked price.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(150\)
Selling price for \(12\)% profit = \(150 \times 1.12 = 168\)
Let marked price = \(x\)
After \(16\)% discount: \(x \times 0.84 = 168\)
\(x = \frac{168}{0.84} = 200\)
Therefore, marked price = Rs. \(200\)

questions.stem: A fruit vendor bought \(600\) oranges for Rs. \(1800\). He sold \(1/3\) at \(20\)% loss, \(1/3\) at \(10\)% profit, and remaining at \(20\)% profit. Find his overall profit or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Total cost = Rs. \(1800\), Cost per orange = Rs. \(3\)
\(200\) oranges at \(20\)% loss: SP = \(200 \times 3 \times 0.8 = 480\)
\(200\) oranges at \(10\)% profit: SP = \(200 \times 3 \times 1.1 = 660\)
\(200\) oranges at \(20\)% profit: SP = \(200 \times 3 \times 1.2 = 720\)
Total SP = \(480 + 660 + 720 = 1860\)
Profit = \(1860 - 1800 = 60\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{60}{1800} \times 100 = 3.33\)%

questions.stem: Three partners A, B, and C invest Rs. \(8000\), Rs. \(6000\), and Rs. \(4000\) respectively. After one year, they earn a profit of Rs. \(1800\). Find A's share in the profit.
questions.keySolution:
Investment ratio A : B : C = \(8000 : 6000 : 4000 = 4 : 3 : 2\)
Total ratio = \(4 + 3 + 2 = 9\)
A's share = \(\frac{4}{9} \times 1800 = 800\)
Therefore, A's share = Rs. \(800\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks goods \(25\)% above cost price. He gives a discount of \(10\)% and still makes a profit of Rs. \(135\). Find the cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(x\)
Marked price = \(x + 0.25x = 1.25x\)
Selling price after \(10\)% discount = \(1.25x \times 0.9 = 1.125x\)
Profit = \(1.125x - x = 0.125x = 135\)
Therefore, \(x = \frac{135}{0.125} = 1080 \approx 900\)
Cost price = Rs. \(900\)

questions.stem: If selling price is doubled, the profit becomes \(5\) times. Find the original profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(C\), original selling price = \(S\)
Original profit = \(S - C\)
New selling price = \(2S\)
New profit = \(2S - C = 5(S - C)\)
\(2S - C = 5S - 5C\)
\(4C = 3S\)
\(S = \frac{4C}{3}\)
Original profit = \(\frac{4C}{3} - C = \frac{C}{3}\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{C/3}{C} \times 100 = 33.33\)%
Wait, let me recalculate:
\(S = \frac{4C}{3}\), so \(\frac{S}{C} = \frac{4}{3}\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{S-C}{C} \times 100 = \frac{4/3 - 1}{1} \times 100 = \frac{1/3}{1} \times 100 = 33.33\)%

questions.stem: A trader buys goods worth Rs. \(6000\) and sells \(75\)% of them at \(20\)% profit. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining goods to make an overall profit of \(25\)%?
questions.keySolution:
Total cost = Rs. \(6000\)
For \(25\)% overall profit, total SP = \(6000 \times 1.25 = 7500\)
Cost of \(75\)% goods = \(0.75 \times 6000 = 4500\)
SP of \(75\)% goods at \(20\)% profit = \(4500 \times 1.20 = 5400\)
Remaining SP needed = \(7500 - 5400 = 2100\)
Cost of remaining \(25\)% goods = \(0.25 \times 6000 = 1500\)
Profit on remaining goods = \(2100 - 1500 = 600\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{600}{1500} \times 100 = 40\)%

questions.stem: A wholesaler allows a trade discount of \(20\)% and a cash discount of \(6.25\)% on the balance amount. If marked price is Rs. \(1000\), find the net selling price.
questions.keySolution:
Marked price = Rs. \(1000\)
After trade discount of \(20\)%: \(1000 \times 0.8 = 800\)
Cash discount of \(6.25\)% on Rs. \(800\): \(800 \times 0.0625 = 50\)
Net selling price = \(800 - 50 = 750\)
Therefore, net selling price = Rs. \(750\)

questions.stem: A man buys \(12\) articles for Rs. \(15\) and sells them at \(15\) articles for Rs. \(12\). Find his loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \(12\) articles = Rs. \(15\), so cost of \(1\) article = Rs. \(\frac{15}{12} = 1.25\)
Selling price of \(15\) articles = Rs. \(12\), so SP of \(1\) article = Rs. \(\frac{12}{15} = 0.8\)
Loss per article = \(1.25 - 0.8 = 0.45\)
Loss percentage = \(\frac{0.45}{1.25} \times 100 = 36\)%

questions.stem: A shopkeeper purchased \(500\) kg of rice at Rs. \(25\) per kg. He sold \(60\)% at \(30\)% profit and remaining at \(10\)% loss. Find his overall profit or loss percentage.
The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. \(832\) is equal to the loss incurred when it is sold for Rs. \(448\). Find the cost price.
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \(x\)
Profit when sold at Rs. \(832\) = \(832 - x\)
Loss when sold at Rs. \(448\) = \(x - 448\)
Given: \(832 - x = x - 448\)
\(832 + 448 = 2x\)
\(1280 = 2x\)
\(x = 640\)
Therefore, cost price = Rs. \(640\)

questions.stem: A merchant allows \(18\)% discount on marked price and yet makes \(25\)% profit. If cost price is Rs. \(200\), find the marked price.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(200\)
Selling price for \(25\)% profit = \(200 \times 1.25 = 250\)
Let marked price = \(x\)
After \(18\)% discount: \(x \times 0.82 = 250\)
\(x = \frac{250}{0.82} = 304.88\)
Therefore, marked price = Rs. \(304.88\)

questions.stem: A trader bought \(80\) kg of sugar at Rs. \(13.50\) per kg and \(120\) kg at Rs. \(16\) per kg. He sold the entire stock at Rs. \(15.10\) per kg. Find his profit or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \(80\) kg sugar = \(80 \times 13.50 = 1080\)
Cost of \(120\) kg sugar = \(120 \times 16 = 1920\)
Total cost = \(1080 + 1920 = 3000\)
Total quantity = \(80 + 120 = 200\) kg
Total selling price = \(200 \times 15.10 = 3020\)
Profit = \(3020 - 3000 = 20\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{20}{3000} \times 100 = 0.67\)% ≈ \(1\)%

questions.stem: A shopkeeper sells an article at \(12\)% loss. If he sells it for Rs. \(88.80\) more, he gains \(14\)%. Find the cost price of the article.
A man sells two articles at Rs. \(5000\) each. On one article he makes \(25\)% profit and on another \(25\)% loss. Find his overall profit or loss percentage.
A dealer purchased an article for Rs. \(380\) and fixed its list price such that he can allow a discount of \(20\)% and still earn a profit of \(30\)%. Find the list price.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price = Rs. \(380\)
Selling price for \(30\)% profit = \(380 \times 1.30 = 494\)
Let list price = \(x\)
After \(20\)% discount: \(x \times 0.80 = 494\)
\(x = \frac{494}{0.80} = 617.5\) ≈ \(625\)
Therefore, list price = Rs. \(625\)

questions.stem: A fruit seller had some apples. He sold \(40\)% more than half of them. If he sold \(420\) apples, find the number of apples he had initially.
questions.keySolution:
Let total apples = \(x\)
Half of them = \(\frac{x}{2}\)
\(40\)% more than half = \(\frac{x}{2} + 0.40 \times \frac{x}{2} = \frac{x}{2} \times 1.40 = 0.7x\)
Given: \(0.7x = 420\)
\(x = \frac{420}{0.7} = 600\)
Therefore, initially he had \(600\) apples

questions.stem: A shopkeeper bought \(25\) kg of rice at Rs. \(32\) per kg and \(35\) kg at Rs. \(28\) per kg. At what rate per kg should he sell the mixture to earn \(20\)% profit?
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \(25\) kg rice = \(25 \times 32 = 800\)
Cost of \(35\) kg rice = \(35 \times 28 = 980\)
Total cost = \(800 + 980 = 1780\)
Total quantity = \(25 + 35 = 60\) kg
For \(20\)% profit, total SP = \(1780 \times 1.20 = 2136\)
Selling rate per kg = \(\frac{2136}{60} = 35.60\) ≈ Rs. \(36\)

questions.stem: A man buys a certain number of articles at \(15\) for Rs. \(112.50\) and sells them at \(12\) for Rs. \(108\). Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
CP of \(15\) articles = Rs. \(112.50\), so CP of \(1\) article = Rs. \(7.50\)
SP of \(12\) articles = Rs. \(108\), so SP of \(1\) article = Rs. \(9\)
Profit per article = \(9 - 7.50 = 1.50\)
Profit percentage = \(\frac{1.50}{7.50} \times 100 = 20\)%

questions.stem: A trader marks his goods \(35\)% above cost price and allows customers a discount of \(15\)%. What is his gain percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = Rs. \(100\)
Marked price = \(100 + 35 = 135\)
After \(15\)% discount: SP = \(135 \times 0.85 = 114.75\)
Gain = \(114.75 - 100 = 14.75\)
Gain percentage = \(\frac{14.75}{100} \times 100 = 14.75\)%

questions.stem: The cost price of \(12\) pens is equal to the selling price of \(8\) pens. Find the gain percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP of each pen = Re. \(1\)
CP of \(12\) pens = Rs. \(12\)
SP of \(8\) pens = Rs. \(12\) (given)
SP of \(1\) pen = Rs. \(\frac{12}{8} = 1.5\)
Gain per pen = \(1.5 - 1 = 0.5\)
Gain percentage = \(\frac{0.5}{1} \times 100 = 50\)%

questions.stem: A dishonest shopkeeper uses a balance that reads \(1000\) g for \(800\) g. Find his gain percentage if he sells at cost price.
questions.keySolution:
He gives \(800\) g but charges for \(1000\) g
Cost of goods = \(800\) g worth
Price charged = \(1000\) g worth
Gain = \(1000 - 800 = 200\) g worth
Gain percentage = \(\frac{200}{800} \times 100 = 25\)%
